summary: Cape Flattery Airport (CQP) is a small regional airstrip located on the Cape York Peninsula in far north Queensland, Australia. It primarily serves the nearby Cape Flattery silica sand mine, one of the largest silica sand mining operations in the world. The airport provides essential access for mine workers and supports charter flights in this remote tropical coastal region.
faqs:
Q: Where is Cape Flattery Airport located?
A: It is situated on the Cape York Peninsula in far north Queensland, Australia, near the Cape Flattery silica sand mining operation along the tropical coast.

Q: Is Cape Flattery Airport open to the public?
A: The airport is primarily a private facility serving the mining industry and is not typically used for regular commercial passenger flights.

Q: What is the main purpose of this airport?
A: It supports the Cape Flattery silica sand mine, facilitating staff transport and occasional charter operations in this isolated region.

Q: How remote is the area around Cape Flattery Airport?
A: The surrounding region is extremely remote, characterized by dense tropical vegetation, limited road access, and proximity to the Great Barrier Reef coastline.
transport_tips: Access to Cape Flattery Airport is almost exclusively by charter or company-arranged flights, as there are no scheduled commercial services. The nearest major town with broader transport links is Cairns, located several hundred kilometers to the south. Road access to the area is limited and often requires four-wheel-drive vehicles due to rough, unsealed tracks.
local_tip: If visiting the region, be aware that the tropical climate brings intense heat and humidity during the wet season (November to April), and crocodile warnings apply near any waterways—always check local conditions before exploring the surrounding wilderness.
